stem: A nurse is interpreting the baseline fetal heart rate during labor. Which baseline range is considered normal in the standardized three-tier intrapartum interpretation system?
rationale: ACOG's current intrapartum fetal heart-rate nomenclature defines a normal baseline fetal heart rate as 110–160 beats/min. Therefore D is correct. A includes rates below the normal lower boundary, B extends below and above the normal range, and C excludes normal values from 110–119 while extending above the normal upper boundary.
educational_objective: Recognize 110–160 beats/min as the normal baseline fetal heart-rate range used in standardized intrapartum interpretation.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
source_document_title: Intrapartum Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring: Interpretation and Management — Clinical Practice Guideline No. 10
source_locator: Table 1, Electronic Fetal Monitoring Definitions — Baseline fetal heart rate; Figure 1, three-tiered category system.
source_claim_supported: ACOG's standardized intrapartum fetal heart-rate nomenclature uses 110–160 beats/min as the normal baseline range within the three-tier interpretation framework.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity → Reduction of Risk Potential; diagnostic/monitoring data and recognition of potential complications.

source_original.stem: A nurse is interpreting the baseline fetal heart rate during labor. Which baseline range is considered normal in the standardized three-tier intrapartum interpretation system?
source_original.rationale: ACOG's fetal heart tracing definitions identify a normal baseline fetal heart rate as 110–160 beats/min and use the three-tier Category I/II/III framework. Option D is therefore correct. Option A includes values below the bradycardia threshold. Option B widens both the lower and upper limits beyond the standard range. Option C excludes normal values from 110–119 and includes values above the tachycardia threshold. Currentness was rechecked against ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 10 from October 2025, which continues to use the three-tier intrapartum classification framework.
source_original.source_detail: ACOG fetal heart tracing definitions — normal baseline 110–160 beats/min and three-tier Category I/II/III framework; currentness checked against Clinical Practice Guideline No. 10 on intrapartum FHR monitoring. correction_summary: Clinical content and keyed answer were retained. Source metadata was upgraded from the older ACOG educational page to the current ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 10 (October 2025), with the exact locator at Table 1 and the three-tier framework figure.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current official ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 10.
audit_findings.currentness: ACOG CPG No. 10 is dated October 2025 and remains the current ACOG intrapartum FHR guideline as checked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Table 1 identifies the baseline FHR definitions; Figure 1 displays the three-tiered category system.
audit_findings.claim_audit: The item tests only the normal baseline range; no additional threshold, intervention, or timing rule was introduced.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because it includes values below the normal lower limit.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because it extends both below and above the normal range.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because it excludes normal 110–119 values and includes values above 160.
distractor_audit.D: Uniquely matches the ACOG normal baseline range.

audit_findings.cueing: All choices are plausible numeric ranges of similar structure and length.
audit_findings.blueprint: Fits Reduction of Risk Potential through interpretation of monitoring data and recognition of abnormal findings.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Second-pass review rechecked the 110–160 range against current ACOG guidance and found no competing answer or unsupported precision.
